purpose: Conversational capability queries for evaluating vocabulary-mismatch retrieval. Written 2026-09-07 from the curated capability inventory BEFORE any fix was designed, and BEFORE any of them were run through search, so the HELDOUT half is a genuine held-out set. DEV is the only half consulted while iterating.
rule: Never move a query between splits. Never edit a HELDOUT query after seeing its result. If HELDOUT needs changing, the change is a new eval set with a new date.

dev.q: make me a picture of a cat wearing a hat
pull the pricing table off this website
how much could i rent my house for
how much is apple stock right now
transcribe this podcast episode for me
write me a song about summer
check if this person is on a sanctions list
is it going to rain tomorrow
run this python snippet and show me the output
take a picture of this webpage
what is the square root of 1764
who is hiring engineers right now
where is this ip address located

remove the background from this photo

adjacent_note: Third battery, added 2026-09-07 after codex round 5. The other two batteries are blind to the class the curated prior actually costs: an intent whose correct answer is a marketplace listing WHILE a curated tool shares generic vocabulary but does something different. Written from the curated inventory by asking, for each curated tool, 'what request shares its words but wants something else?' — before running any of them.

adjacent.q: find an available domain name to register

astra_note: Fourth battery, from the gpt-6-astra audits (rounds 8 and 9, 2026-09-08). These are the cases seven codex rounds and three hand-written batteries all missed. Several remain OPEN by decision, not oversight - see report.md 'What is not fixed'.

astra.status: OPEN — builtwith/free ranks first; the gate that fixes it costs a curated win

astra.q: look for linkedin profiles by name
astra.status: OPEN on small tenant catalogs — 'linkedin' is excluded as capability vocabulary because clado/linkedin-profile uses the word

astra.q: use Acme Search to search for matching documents
astra.status: FIXED — tenant-owned provider names now matched as a per-request overlay. Only scorable with a synthetic tenant row: the static-index scorer in harness/ cannot see tenantOwned providers, so it reports this as a miss. The gate test 'honours a caller who names a provider the tenant brought' is what actually covers it.

astra.q: check an available company domain name
astra.status: OPEN - builtwith/domain takes rank 1. The prior reorders rows whose own scores did not change, which is the P1 that falsified 'never worse than today'.
OPEN - DeepSeek normalizes to 'deep seek', so a native integration's name makes 'seek' capability vocabulary. Needs an explicit brand marker.

OPEN - 'GitHub' normalizes to 'git hub' and matches neither the registered name 'github' nor the host. Needs consistent spelling normalization. Reproduces on 333 native rows + GitHub's 10 endpoints; the full index masks it.

astra.q: generate an image of the numbers from a text prompt
astra.status: FIXED round 9 - stop words are stripped before the single-word brand disqualifier, so 'The Numbers' no longer escapes it.

astra_scoring_note: Scored on the FULL static index by harness/mcp-eval-batteries.local.test.ts: 3/7 @1, 6/7 @5. Three cases do not reproduce in that shape and are not scorable there: 'use Acme Search' needs a tenant-owned row (gate test covers it), and 'look for linkedin profiles by name' and 'look up GitHub projects' reproduce on a restricted catalog (333 native rows plus the one provider's endpoints), which is closer to a real tenant's enabled subset than the full index is. Read the per-case status, not the aggregate.
